# Configuration

Plugin ID: `utilities.local`. Options live on the `plugins` entry in `opencode.json`. An invalid option fails setup with `OPTIONS_INVALID` and names every offending key. Values are not echoed.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [{
    "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-utilities#v0.0.2",
    "options": {
      "modules": { "weather": true, "time": true, "speech": true },
      "stateRoot": "<absolute path>",
      "speech": { "assetsDir": "<absolute path>" },
      "allowUntestedHost": false
    }
  }]
}
```

There is no `policy` option and no `allowActions` option. Permissions are OpenCode rules, described below.

## Options

| Key | Type | Default | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modules.weather` | boolean | `true` | When `false`, weather tools are not registered. |
| `modules.time` | boolean | `true` | When `false`, time and timer tools are not registered. |
| `modules.speech` | boolean | `true` | When `false`, speech tools are not registered and `/utilities-speech-install` refuses. |
| `stateRoot` | absolute path | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode-utilities`, or `~/.local/share/opencode-utilities` | Timer stores and the default speech output directory. Must be mode `0700` and owned by the user. See [Symbolic links](#symbolic-links). |
| `speech.assetsDir` | absolute path | unset | Flat pre-seed directory. See [Speech files](#speech-files). |
| `allowUntestedHost` | boolean | `false` | When `true`, an OpenCode version outside `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0` loads, and status shows `host untested` with a warning. When `false` or omitted, setup throws for such a version. |

Unknown keys are rejected. A relative path is rejected.

`stateRoot` layout:

| Path under `stateRoot` | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `projects/<scope>/timers` | This project's SQLite timer store. `<scope>` is a hash of OpenCode's project ID, so every folder of a project shares one store. |
| `speech/<scope>/<id>.wav` | This project's default synthesis files. Removed at startup when older than 7 days. |
| `jobs/job-*` | Per-call scratch. Removed at startup when older than 10 minutes. |

Timers are per project: a timer set at the project root is the same timer in every subfolder. OpenCode's project is the git repository; a folder outside any repository belongs to OpenCode's shared `global` project.

The caches are not under `stateRoot`. They are under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/opencode-utilities` (`~/.cache/opencode-utilities` when unset):

| Path under the cache | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `<sha256>/<name>` | Speech engine and model files. |
| `weather/weather-signal/<hash>.json` | Open-Meteo responses, one file per request URL, mode `0600` in a `0700` folder. A forecast is reused for 30 minutes and a place search for 30 days, so repeated calls cost no extra requests. Files older than 31 days are removed at startup. |

### Symbolic links

At startup the plugin resolves each of its roots once with `realpath`: `stateRoot`, the cache, `speech.assetsDir` and the installed package. A link above a root, or the root itself, is fine. Examples are macOS `/tmp` (a link to `/private/tmp`), Fedora Atomic and Silverblue `/home` (a link to `/var/home`), and a dotfile setup that links `~/.local` or `~/.cache`. Status shows the resolved paths.

Inside those roots, the plugin refuses every symbolic link: a timer store, a job folder, a cached or pre-seeded speech file, a program. The error is `UNSAFE_PATH`, never `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH`.

## Host check

`package.json` states `"opencode": { "host": ">=2.2.3 <2.3.0" }`. Setup compares `ctx.app.version` with that range.

| Version | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6 | Load. These are the tested releases: status shows `tested`, and the status RPC `host.tested` is `true`. |
| 2.2.99 or a later 2.2 release | Load normally, untested. The OpenCode row shows `untested; supported range >=2.2.3 <2.3.0` and `host.tested` is `false`; `state` and the next step are unchanged. |
| 2.2.2, 2.3.0, 3.0.0, a prerelease, a dev build, `unknown` | Refused: setup fails, so there is no status. With `allowUntestedHost: true` the plugin loads, and the next step is a warning. |

Do not write the range as `^2.2.3`. That would accept 2.3.

The refusal text is: `HOST_UNTESTED: Utilities supports OpenCode >=2.2.3 <2.3.0, found <version>. Next step: Use OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 or 2.2.6, or set the plugin option allowUntestedHost: true to run anyway.`

## Tools

Effective name `utilities_<name>`. `options.permission` is that name, so a deny with resource `*` hides the tool. Code Mode is on. None are pinned: the skills hold the call shapes, and `search({ namespace: "utilities", query })` finds a tool.

Only available modules are registered. Transcription and synthesis stay registered while their files are merely missing, so the first call can ask to download them. A disabled module, an unsupported platform, or a failed integrity check does not register that module's tools. Availability changes (a finished download, for example) reload the tool list.

| Tool | Effect | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `utilities_status` | compute | none |
| `utilities_time_now`, `utilities_time_zones`, `utilities_time_zone_info`, `utilities_time_convert`, `utilities_time_calendar`, `utilities_time_add`, `utilities_time_between`, `utilities_time_format`, `utilities_time_holidays`, `utilities_time_business_days` | compute | none |
| `utilities_timer_get`, `utilities_timer_list`, `utilities_timer_check` | read-state | none |
| `utilities_timer_set`, `utilities_timer_delete` | write-state | ask. Resource `timer:<name>`, save `timer:*`. |
| `utilities_weather_geocode`, `utilities_weather_current`, `utilities_weather_daily`, `utilities_weather_hourly`, `utilities_weather_demand_signal`, `utilities_weather_summary` | network | ask. Resource and save are the provider hosts. `metadata.location` is the place or query. |
| `utilities_speech_transcribe` | read-file | host `read`, and `external_directory` when the file is outside the location and the project |
| `utilities_speech_synthesize` | write-file | ask `utilities_speech_synthesize`. Resource `kitten-nano-int8/<voice>`, save `*`. A given `path` also asserts `edit`, and `external_directory` outside the project. |

`utilities_speech_download` is not a tool. It is the action asserted before a download, by the first transcription or synthesis call that needs files and by `/utilities-speech-install`. Resource and save are the release host (`github.com`). `metadata.bytes` is the total size. `metadata.files` lists the names.

### Holidays and regions

Holiday data is offline, from the `holidays` crate, and covers 2000–2030. Some rows are regional. In the UK (`GB`), a row may apply to only England, Wales, Scotland or Northern Ireland, which the data marks in the name, as in `Summer Bank Holiday [Scotland]`. The Isle of Man (`IM`) data repeats those UK rows. No other country in the data has regional rows; a bracket there holds an English name, as in `Año nuevo [New Year's Day]`.

- Every holiday in a result has `nationwide` (boolean) and `regions` (the nations, empty when nationwide). A row that joins a regional and a nationwide holiday on one date is nationwide.
- `utilities_time_holidays` lists and checks every holiday, regional ones included. With `region`, it keeps only that nation's holidays and the nationwide ones, and `check` answers `is_holiday: false` for another nation's holiday.
- `utilities_time_business_days` skips weekends (Saturday and Sunday) and, with `country`, the nationwide holidays. With `region`, it also skips that nation's own. A count lists the regional weekday holidays it did not skip in `regional_holidays_not_skipped`.
- `region` is only valid with `country: "GB"`. It takes `England`, `Wales`, `Scotland` or `Northern Ireland`.

### File resources

A path is resolved against the location directory. `~` is expanded.

- Inside the location directory, or inside the project directory (the git worktree root) when that directory is not the filesystem root: the `read` or `edit` resource is relative to the location. A file in a parent of the location but still in the project is a resource such as `../audio/in.wav`. `external_directory` is not asserted.
- Outside both: `external_directory` is asserted first, resource `<parent>/*`, saved as `<repository root of that parent, or the parent>/*`. Then `read` or `edit` is asserted on the absolute path.

The transcription source is identified before the prompt. It must be a regular file of at most 20 MiB, not a symbolic link. A file swapped while the prompt is open is refused. WAV ancillary chunks are accepted. The format is PCM16, one or two channels, 8–48 kHz, at most ten minutes.

### Weather sign-in

Integration ID `open-meteo`, method `key`, label "Open-Meteo commercial API key".

- No connection: free tier, non-commercial, rate-limited. Hosts `api.open-meteo.com` and `geocoding-api.open-meteo.com`.
- Connected key: commercial tier. Hosts `customer-api.open-meteo.com` and `customer-geocoding-api.open-meteo.com`. The key is the child environment variable `OPEN_METEO_API_KEY`, never an argument.
- Adding a key: run `/connect` and choose Open-Meteo; in the TUI, press `o` or Enter on it, then paste the key. On the CLI, `opencode auth login open-meteo` prompts for the key.
- Rejected key: `/connect` shows Open-Meteo as "Sign in required", and status says so. Next step: run `/connect` and choose Open-Meteo, then enter a valid key, or run `opencode auth logout open-meteo` to return to the free tier.

There is no `env` method.

Every weather output includes `attribution` with the value `Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0)`, and `cache`: `miss` for a fresh request, `hit` when the response came from the weather cache (see `stateRoot` layout above). The cache is shared by every project of this user. A connected key is never stored in it; requests with a key are cached apart from free-tier ones.

## Permissions

Default ask rules are inserted by `ctx.agent.transform`, immediately after each agent's base `{ "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" }`. This is the only mechanism. User rules and saved approvals win because they are evaluated later. A deny that comes later, including Plan's, is not weakened.

```jsonc
[
  { "action": "utilities_weather_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
  { "action": "utilities_timer_set", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
  { "action": "utilities_timer_delete", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
  { "action": "utilities_speech_synthesize", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
  { "action": "utilities_speech_download", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }
]
```

Every rule needs `"resource"`. Without it, OpenCode skips the rule.

### Allow and deny

Top-level `permissions` apply to every agent. OpenCode adds them after the agent's built-in rules and this plugin's ask rules, and before the agent's own `permissions` from your config. The last matching rule wins. An allow there skips the prompt for Build, and it also allows the action for Plan and Explore, whose restrictions are built in. Put an allow on one agent when a stricter agent must stay strict.

```jsonc
{
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "utilities_weather_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "utilities_timer_set", "resource": "timer:*", "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "utilities_timer_delete", "resource": "timer:*", "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "utilities_speech_synthesize", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "utilities_speech_download", "resource": "github.com", "effect": "allow" }
  ]
}
```

`utilities_timer_*` and `utilities_speech_*` also match, as in the README. A deny hides the tools:

```jsonc
{ "action": "utilities_speech_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }
```

A saved "Always allow" is project-wide. It applies to every agent in that project, Plan included. A directory with no git commit can belong to OpenCode's shared `global` project, so an approval saved there applies in every such directory. See [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md).

### Agents without the inserted rules

OpenCode creates agents that are defined only in user config, and agents added by later plugins, after this plugin's transform. They do not receive the ask rules. Status names such an agent only when its own rules would run a Utilities side effect (weather, a timer change, synthesis or the download) without asking: the last rule that matches is an allow. An agent whose rules ask or deny for all of them, such as one ending in `{ "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }`, needs no fix and is not listed.

Status's next step is: Put the default rules shown by /utilities-status first in each listed agent's own permissions, in opencode.json or the agent's Markdown file, followed by your top-level rules for Utilities tools. That is, the block above goes **first** in that agent's own `permissions`, followed by any `utilities_*` rules you already have in the top-level `permissions`.

```jsonc
{
  "agents": {
    "reviewer": {
      "permissions": [
        { "action": "utilities_weather_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
        { "action": "utilities_timer_set", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
        { "action": "utilities_timer_delete", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
        { "action": "utilities_speech_synthesize", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
        { "action": "utilities_speech_download", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
        { "action": "utilities_weather_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The last rule in that example is one you already had at the top level, repeated so it still wins for this agent. Omit it if you have no such rule.

Do not put the ask block in the top-level `permissions`. That would loosen Explore.

For a Markdown agent, the same array goes in the `permissions` front matter.

### Non-interactive runs

`opencode run` auto-rejects a prompt. Stderr:

```text
permission requested: utilities_weather_current (api.open-meteo.com, geocoding-api.open-meteo.com); auto-rejecting
```

The model is told: "This non-interactive run cannot ask the user for permission, so the request was rejected. Continue without this action."

`--auto` approves asks and does not override a deny. Allow rules, as above, skip the prompt. Pre-seed speech files in CI so the job does not need a download.

## Commands, RPC and TUI

| Surface | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `utilities_status` | Returns the status object, with the agents without default rules as a count and one next step. Compute. Does not ask. |
| `/utilities-status` | Posts the full status into the session: the rows Connection, Account, Access, the modules, Skills, Tools, Agents without default rules (names, then the block, one rule per line), OpenCode, and one Next step (`Nothing to do.` when nothing is needed). |
| `/utilities-install` | Asserts `utilities_native_download` for each time or weather program that is not cached, then downloads it and checks its size and SHA-256 against the release manifest. A refusal downloads nothing. |
| `/utilities-speech-install` | Asserts `utilities_speech_download`, then downloads missing files. |
| `/utilities` | TUI dialog, palette "Utilities: Status". Reads the `status` RPC method only, when it opens, and on server, agent and Open-Meteo key events, which it hears only while open. Shows the same lines as `/utilities-status`. `r` refreshes, `Esc` closes. The key hint reads `r refresh · esc close`. |
| RPC `status` | The `utilities.local` RPC's only method. Returns the same status object. The TUI imports its contract from its own bundle; the package does not export it. The id the plugin had before the rename, `utilities.tools`, answers the same method until the next minor release, and status then says it is deprecated. |
| RPC `utilities.local.tools` | The tools RPC for scripts: `describe`, plus one method per tool, run as a session and its agent. Every tool is allowed by default; `access` and a script's own rules restrict it. A call resolves the rule before dispatch: an ask is refused, not prompted, and only an allow runs. See [scripting.md](scripting.md). The old id `utilities.tools.tools` answers the same methods until the next minor release, and its `describe` carries `"deprecated": "use utilities.local.tools"`. |

The status RPC starts with the fields every one of these plugins shares:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | The plugin's version. |
| `host` | `{ version, range, tested }`: OpenCode's version, the supported range `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`, and whether the version is a tested release (2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6). `next` is added only for a version outside the range that runs because of `allowUntestedHost`. |
| `state` | `ready`; `failed` when every module that is on failed; `disabled` when every module is off. Utilities has no status-only mode, so the shared `host_untested` never occurs: an untested host shows only in `host.tested` and the OpenCode row. |
| `unguardedAgents` | The agents without the default rules whose own rules would run a Utilities side effect without asking. Always present; `[]` when none. |
| `nextStep` | Exactly the `Next step` row; `Nothing to do.` when nothing is needed. Missing speech files that download on first use, and the free weather tier, never set it. |

Then Utilities' own: the platform, per-module availability, the weather tier and key, speech file states (`missing`, `cached` or `pre-seeded`), voices, whether files are pre-seeded, the cache and output directories, the due timer count and the timer store, `shadowedSkills` (each `{ name, path }`: a skill with one of the plugin's skill ids, such as one in `.opencode/skills/utilities-time/`, that OpenCode loads instead of the plugin's own; `[]` when none), and the ask-by-default actions. An item's own `next` is its own next step. The `utilities_status` tool has the same fields, with `unguardedAgents` as a count. For those agents, `nextStep` is: Put the default rules shown by /utilities-status first in each listed agent's own permissions, in opencode.json or the agent's Markdown file, followed by your top-level rules for Utilities tools.

## Bounds

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Tool input / structured output | 32 KiB / 64 KiB |
| Native stdout / stderr | 1 MiB / 64 KiB |
| Deadline, after approval | time 10 s, weather 45 s, speech 120 s |
| Queue waiting | time 32, weather 16, speech 4 |
| Concurrent calls | time 4, weather 2, speech 1 |
| Timer store | 1,000 records. Name 128 characters. Description 2 KiB. 16 tags. |
| Holiday data | 2000–2030, offline |
| Calendar dates | 1900–2100 |
| Business-day window | at most 366 days |
| Speech text | 5,000 characters |
| Transcription | PCM16 WAV, 8–48 kHz, mono or stereo, 20 MiB, ten minutes. Ancillary chunks accepted. Not a symbolic link. |
| Synthesis WAV | at most 50 MiB. Default files older than 7 days are removed at startup. |

`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` is distinct from `CANCELLED`. The deadline does not include time spent waiting for permission.

## Errors

A tool failure is `Tool.Error` with `message` set to `CODE: what happened. Next step: What to do.` and `metadata.code` plus `metadata.hint`. Host permission errors propagate unchanged and have no plugin code. Every code the plugin raises is in this table, and a unit test checks that both lists match.

| Code | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| `OPTIONS_INVALID` | Fix the named option in the Utilities plugin options in `opencode.json`. |
| `STATUS_UNAVAILABLE` | Run `/utilities-status` in a session to see the error, or check the OpenCode server log. |
| `SKILLS_INVALID` | A skill file is missing or malformed; setup skips it with this warning. Reinstall the plugin. |
| `HOST_UNTESTED` | OpenCode is outside `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`. Use 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 or 2.2.6, or set `allowUntestedHost`. |
| `DISABLED` | Set `modules.<name>` to `true`. |
| `CLOSED` | The plugin is shutting down. Retry after OpenCode has reloaded it. |
| `NATIVE_FILES_MISSING` | The time or weather program is not downloaded yet, or this copy of the plugin has no release manifest. Call the tool with permission to download it, or run `/utilities-install`. In a checkout, run `npm run native:ensure`. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM` | No build for this platform. Time and weather are unaffected when only speech lacks an engine. |
| `BINARY_MISSING`, `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH` | A program or speech file is missing or is not the pinned file. Call the tool again: a program is downloaded again after its permission. For speech, delete the cache and run `/utilities-speech-install`. |
| `CONTRACT_MISMATCH` | The plugin's files, or a program's output, do not match this version. Reinstall; if it persists, report it with the `utilities_status` output. |
| `SPEECH_ASSETS_MISSING` | Approve the download, run `/utilities-speech-install`, or pre-seed. |
| `DOWNLOAD_FAILED` | Check the network and retry, or pre-seed the speech files. |
| `INPUT_INVALID` | Correct the named field. The message names the rule, such as the 2000–2030 holiday range, never the value. |
| `INPUT_LIMIT`, `OUTPUT_LIMIT` | The input is over 32 KiB, or the result over 64 KiB. Send less, or narrow the request (fewer days, hours or results). |
| `QUEUE_FULL` | Wait, then retry. Each module has its own queue. |
| `CANCELLED` | The call was cancelled. Call the tool again if you still need the result. |
| `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` | The call ran past its time limit (see [Bounds](#bounds)). Retry, or narrow the request. |
| `SPAWN_FAILED` | The program behind the tool could not start. Call `utilities_status`; reinstall if a module is unavailable. |
| `BACKEND_FAILED` | A program reported another error. For weather the message says which: no such place, the rate limit, or a failed request. |
| `BACKEND_JSON_INVALID`, `STDOUT_LIMIT`, `STDERR_LIMIT` | The program's output was unreadable or too large. Narrow the request and retry; if it persists, reinstall. |
| `TIME_NONEXISTENT` | The local time is skipped by a daylight-saving change in `from_timezone`. Use a time outside the change, or add the UTC offset the user means. |
| `TIME_AMBIGUOUS` | The local time happens twice at a daylight-saving change. The message gives both UTC offsets and instants. Add the offset the user means, or ask which one. |
| `TIME_OFFSET_MISMATCH` | The `datetime` has an offset that `from_timezone` does not use at that moment. Remove it, or use the zone's own. |
| `HOLIDAY_COVERAGE` | The call needs holiday data outside 2000–2030, for example the next business day after 2030-12-31. Use dates in range, or leave out `country` to count weekends only. |
| `TIME_OUT_OF_RANGE` | The result is outside what the time engine supports. Use a smaller amount or a nearer date. |
| `TIMER_EXISTS` | Ask the user whether to overwrite it; then `utilities_timer_set` with `replace: true`, or another name. |
| `TIMER_NOT_FOUND` | `utilities_timer_list`. |
| `TIMER_QUOTA`, `TIMER_BYTE_QUOTA` | The project has 1,000 timers, or its store is full. Delete timers, or use shorter descriptions and tags. |
| `TIMER_STATE_UNKNOWN` | Read the timer before retrying. The change may or may not have been saved. |
| `STATE_FILE_UNSAFE` | A timer store file is a link or not a regular file. Remove it from the project's timer directory. |
| `WEATHER_KEY_REJECTED` | Reconnect, or log out for the free tier. |
| `SOURCE_REJECTED` | A regular `.wav` file, not a symbolic link, at most 20 MiB. |
| `SOURCE_CHANGED` | The audio file changed while the call waited for approval. Call the tool again. |
| `WAV_INVALID`, `WAV_UNSUPPORTED` | Convert to 16-bit PCM WAV. The hint includes an `ffmpeg` example. |
| `AUDIO_DURATION_LIMIT` | The audio is over ten minutes. Split it into shorter files. |
| `SPEECH_FAILED` | The speech engine failed; the message names the engine's code. Retry; if it persists, call `utilities_status`. |
| `BRIDGE_CORRELATION`, `OUTPUT_PATH_MISMATCH` | The speech engine answered another request, or wrote somewhere unexpected. Retry; if it persists, delete the speech cache and run `/utilities-speech-install`. |

| `UNSAFE_PATH` | A file or folder inside the plugin's own directories is a symbolic link, or not the expected type. Replace the link with the real file or folder, or reinstall. Links above those directories are fine. See [Symbolic links](#symbolic-links). |

# In Jelly

[Jelly](https://heyjelly.ai) runs OpenCode agents. It reads the `jelly` section of this
package's `package.json` as JSON, without loading the plugin, when a person reviews the exact
version, and uses it as follows.

Jelly names the plugin **Utilities** (`jelly.title`), with the package name and version beneath. Under
that name it shows the one line in `jelly.summary`, and beside it the mark in `jelly.icon`
(`assets/icon.svg`, shipped in the package): Jelly reads that file once, when it records the
plugin, and keeps it only if it is a clean SVG of drawing elements, with no script, style, link
or outside reference. A Jelly whose declaration schema lacks `summary` or `icon` refuses this
declaration, because that schema accepts no unknown keys.

## Tools and permissions

24 tools are declared (21 read-only): every tool the plugin registers. Jelly's agents have no base "allow everything"
rule, so this plugin's own default rules, which it puts after that rule, never reach them. Every tool is allowed by
default, the speech download included, so those agents run everything Utilities offers; the person restricts it with
Jelly's own tool settings, or with this plugin's `access` option where the plugin's rules do apply. Jelly
writes each declared `ask` or `deny` as that tool's default instead (the person's own choice
replaces it), and denies a read-only helper every tool not marked `readOnly`. A declared `allow`
changes nothing in Jelly.

- Ask: none: every declared tool is allowed.
- Off: none.

Weather sends a place to Open-Meteo and is read-only by class; `utilities_speech_download` is not declared: it is not a
tool but the consent the speech tools assert before a download, and Jelly's declaration has no place for a permission. To make the changes ask instead, set `access: "ask-changes"` in
the plugin options.

The declaration lists the tools of this version. Keep `jelly.tools` in step with the tool table in
`src/domain/contract.ts`; `test/unit/jelly.test.ts` checks each declared effect against the plugin's own
default rules, and the list and its `readOnly` marks against that table.

## Skills

Declared: `utilities-time`, `utilities-weather`, `utilities-speech`. Jelly refuses an install whose
skill ids collide with another plugin's or the agent's own.

## Views and scripts

None: `jelly.views` and `jelly.rpc` are empty.

## Signing in

Nothing is required. `jelly.signIns` declares one optional sign-in, `open-meteo`: OpenCode's key integration for Open-Meteo's commercial key (`required: false`). The free tier works without it, so the card stays Connected and the row reads Optional, with a link to Open-Meteo's pricing. A key that Open-Meteo turns down shows this plugin's `needs_auth` message on the row, with Replace the key.

Jelly folds the declared sign-ins into this plugin's one card, which shows each as Connected, Not signed in or Sign in again (expired or revoked), and starts, renews and signs out of each. An agent's `jelly_connection_request`, or a tool result that names this plugin's "Run /connect and choose …" next step, opens the same card. The plugin still signs in through OpenCode, as it does without Jelly; the declaration only tells Jelly which of the engine's integrations and servers are this plugin's.

## Settings

`jelly.contributes.settings` declares one setting, `access`, the option of the same name, as a choice of three:
**Allowed** (`all`, the default), **Ask before changes** (`ask-changes`) and **Read only** (`read-only`), with Jelly's
own line for each. Jelly draws it as a choice, never as free text, and saves only one of the three, the options
parser's own set. A Jelly that does not know declared choices (before app#1301) refuses the whole declaration.
`test/unit/jelly.test.ts` checks the setting against Jelly's setting rules, restated in `test/support/jelly-settings.ts`,
and each declared value against the options parser.

## Versions

Jelly's curated catalogue pins an exact version. Each release is published under a new version, so a review in
Jelly can tell the two apart.

The declaration test runs the shared kit, `test/support/jelly-kit.ts`, which checks the declaration and this page against Jelly's plugin authors' standard. `scripts/check-copies.mjs` holds the kit, Jelly's setting rules (`test/support/jelly-settings.ts`) and the shared part of the tools RPC (`src/host/tools-rpc.ts`), equal to the copies every plugin carries.

# Scripting

Unofficial plugin. Not affiliated with OpenCode or Open-Meteo.

A script can call Utilities' tools with no model: a cron job, a shell script, or any program that can reach the OpenCode
server. It uses the tools RPC, `utilities.local.tools`, through `opencode api` or an OpenCode client.

The envelope is
`opencode api post /api/rpc/utilities.local.tools/<method> -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{…}}}'`.

The id before the rename, `utilities.tools.tools`, still answers the same methods, and its `describe` carries
`"deprecated": "use utilities.local.tools"`: move a script to the new id before the next minor release, when the old one
goes. The status command says so once an old id has been called.

| Methods | The tools | Class |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `utilities_status`: the compact status, with the unguarded agents as a count | read |
| `time_now`, `time_zones`, `time_zone_info`, `time_convert`, `time_calendar`, `time_add`, `time_between`, `time_format`, `time_holidays`, `time_business_days` | the ten time tools | read |
| `timer_set` | sets a timer in the project | write |
| `timer_get`, `timer_list`, `timer_check` | the timer reads | read |
| `timer_delete` | deletes a timer | write |
| `weather_geocode`, `weather_current`, `weather_daily`, `weather_hourly`, `weather_demand_signal`, `weather_summary` | the six weather tools | read |
| `speech_transcribe` | transcription | read |
| `speech_synthesize` | writes a WAV file | export |
| `describe` | none: lists the methods, their classes, permission actions, whether each can run here now, and each tool's input and output as JSON Schema | – |

Every tool is a method. Each runs the tool's own path, with the same input, the same checks and the same permission
requests as the tool the model calls. The class says the worst thing a method can do; it never decides whether a call
runs: the rules do.

A result is the tool's own output, as plain JSON: the same object the model's tool returns as its `output`. An
MCP-backed plugin's tools RPC wraps a result as `{ output?, text }`; these methods are the plugin's own, so the result
is the output itself.

## A script runs as a session

Every call names a session, and the session must name an agent. The script runs as that agent, with exactly the access
its model would have:

- The call resolves the tool's action, `utilities_<name>` on `*`, against the agent's rules and then the session's, with
  the host's order (the last matching rule wins). Only an `allow` runs. An `ask` is refused, because no one is there to
  answer the prompt, and a `deny` is refused; both cost nothing: no tool call and no prompt left waiting.
- The tool then asks for what it needs, as it does for the model: weather asks for `utilities_weather_<tool>` on the
  Open-Meteo hosts, transcription asks for `read` (and `external_directory` outside the project), and the first speech
  call asks for `utilities_speech_download`, which is also refused unless the session allows it.
- The default rules allow every tool, so a script runs a read or a change unless the user restricts the plugin: the
  `access` option's `"ask-changes"` makes an ask of the timer writes, synthesis and the speech download, and `"read-only"`
  denies them. A script's agent can also narrow it: a rules block of its own, or `access` on the plugin, decides.

Create a session for the script once, with the agent it runs as and the project as its `location`, and keep its id (`data.id` in the result). A session made without a location belongs to the service's default location, where the project's agents may not exist, and each call then fails `Agent not found`.

```sh
opencode api post /api/session -d '{"title":"morning check","agent":"build","location":{"directory":"/path/to/project"}}'
```

A test of a script creates its own session in the same way. Never borrow an existing session found through history or a
session list: the script would run as that session's agent, under that session's rules.

Session rules come after the agent's, so a session can open or narrow what its script may do. This one may call
`weather_current` and `weather_daily`, and nothing else from Utilities that asks:

```sh
opencode api post /api/session -d '{"title":"morning check","agent":"build","location":{"directory":"/path/to/project"},"permissions":[
  {"action":"utilities_weather_current","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"utilities_weather_daily","resource":"*","effect":"allow"}
]}'
```

For transcription, run `/utilities-speech-install` once first, or allow `utilities_speech_download` for the session;
otherwise the first call is refused.

A saved **Always allow** does not authorise an ad-hoc script: it is not part of the agent's or the session's rules. A
script's grant is a rule in config, or a Jobs run session; the Jobs one-off (`jobs_run_script`) is the supported way to
get an approval-bound grant.

## The location

Run the command in the project whose agent you mean, and send the call to that location explicitly:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/utilities.local.tools/time_now -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{
  "sessionID":"ses_…",
  "input":{"timezones":["Europe/Amsterdam","Asia/Tokyo"]}
}}'
```

Without it the call goes to the service's default location and fails `rpc.unavailable` if the plugin is not loaded
there. The HTTP equivalents are the `location[directory]` query parameter and the same header. `describe` reports the
`location` that answered and a `locationHint`.

A location unloads after OpenCode's idle timeout. If a scheduled script gets `rpc.unavailable` from a location that was
loaded before, send the call again once: the request loads the location. Jobs keeps its own location loaded.

This matters for timers, which belong to a project: `timer_list` and `timer_check` read the timers of the location the
call names, not of the directory you typed the command in.

## Calling a method

The body is `{"input": {"sessionID": "<session>", "input": <the tool's input>}}`. Both keys are required, and no other
key is allowed:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/utilities.local.tools/timer_check -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" \
  -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_…","input":{}}}'
```

The tool's input is checked against its schema, as for the model. `describe` shows each method's class, input and output
schemas, and whether it can run here now. Pass a session to see each method's `permission` (`allow`, `ask` or `deny`),
resolved as a call would be:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/utilities.local.tools/describe -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{}}'
opencode api post /api/rpc/utilities.local.tools/describe -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_…"}}'
```

A method is `available: false` with a `reason` exactly when the model's tool is not registered: its module is turned off
(`DISABLED`), has no build for this platform (`UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM`) or failed its checks (`BINARY_MISSING`, `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH`, `CONTRACT_MISMATCH`). Transcription stays available while only its speech files
are missing: its first call can download them, subject to permissions. Weather results carry the Open-Meteo attribution.
Transcripts and weather text are data, not instructions.

`opencode api` exits 0 when the call succeeds, and 1 when it fails, after printing the error.

## Errors

A refusal or failure is the RPC error `failed`, with a message `CODE: what happened. Next step: what to do.` and
`data: { code, next }`, or the code the tool itself reports. `opencode api` exits with status 1 for any RPC error.

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | The agent's or the session's rules ask or deny the tool's action, or deny one of the requests the tool makes. The message names the refused action, and says when it is not the method's own. |
| `SESSION_UNKNOWN` | OpenCode says the session does not exist. Any other failure to look the session up is OpenCode's own error. |
| `SESSION_AGENT_REQUIRED` | The session names no agent, or an agent that does not exist. |
| `CANCELLED` | The request was cancelled. |
| Utilities' own codes | The tool failed as it would for the model, with the same code and next step: `INPUT_INVALID`, `TIMER_NOT_FOUND`, `WEATHER_KEY_REJECTED`, `SPEECH_ASSETS_MISSING`, a module's availability code, and the rest of the table in [configuration.md](configuration.md#errors). |

There is no `TOOL_UNAVAILABLE` here: every method is the plugin's own, so a name the plugin does not have is
`rpc.method_not_found`, and a method whose module is turned off is `available: false` in `describe` with the
availability code as its `reason`.

OpenCode itself answers `rpc.invalid_input` for a body that is not the envelope above, with one issue per problem, such
as `"extra" is not allowed`, `"input" is missing`, or `describe takes nothing, or {"sessionID":"<session>"}` for
`describe` given anything else. It answers `rpc.method_not_found` for a method that does not exist.

A `PERMISSION_DENIED` refusal names the action that was refused. When that is not the method's own, the message says so,
as in `utilities_speech_transcribe needs utilities_speech_download, which was refused …`.

- **An ask:** the next step names the allow rule to add.
- **A deny rule:** the message says so (`… which a deny rule refuses …`), and the next step says to remove or narrow
  that deny rule in the agent or the session, add a later allow rule to the session, or use another agent.

## What scripts cannot do

- Answer an approval prompt: an `ask` is refused. A write needs a prior allow rule.
- Read the Open-Meteo key: the weather program gets it, the script never does.

A script's calls write nothing to the session, and OpenCode's `execute.before` and `execute.after` tool hooks, from any
plugin, do not run for them.

# misaki Misaki is a G2P engine designed for [Kokoro](https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro) models. Hosted demo: https://hf.co/spaces/hexgrad/Misaki-G2P ### English Usage You can run this in one cell on [Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/): ```py !pip install -q "misaki[en]" from misaki import en g2p = en.G2P(trf=False, british=False, fallback=None) # no transformer, American English text = '[Misaki](/misˈɑki/) is a G2P engine designed for [Kokoro](/kˈOkəɹO/) models.' phonemes, tokens = g2p(text) print(phonemes) # misˈɑki ɪz ə ʤˈitəpˈi ˈɛnʤən dəzˈInd fɔɹ kˈOkəɹO mˈɑdᵊlz. ``` To fallback to espeak: ```py # Installing espeak varies across platforms, this silent install works on Colab: !apt-get -qq -y install espeak-ng > /dev/null 2>&1 !pip install -q "misaki[en]" phonemizer-fork from misaki import en, espeak fallback = espeak.EspeakFallback(british=False) # en-us g2p = en.G2P(trf=False, british=False, fallback=fallback) # no transformer, American English text = 'Now outofdictionary words are handled by espeak.' phonemes, tokens = g2p(text) print(phonemes) # nˈW Wɾɑfdˈɪkʃənˌɛɹi wˈɜɹdz ɑɹ hˈændəld bI ˈispik. ``` ### English - https://github.com/explosion/spaCy - https://github.com/savoirfairelinux/num2words - https://github.com/hexgrad/misaki/blob/main/EN_PHONES.md ### Japanese The second gen Japanese tokenizer now uses pyopenjtalk with full unidic, enabling pitch accent marks and improved phrase merging. Deep gratitude to [@sophiefy](https://github.com/sophiefy) for invaluable recommendations and nuanced help with pitch accent. - https://github.com/r9y9/pyopenjtalk - https://github.com/polm/unidic-py The first gen Japanese tokenizer mainly relies on cutlet => fugashi => mecab => unidic-lite, with each being a wrapper around the next. Deep gratitute to [@Respaired](https://github.com/Respaired) for helping me learn the ropes of Japanese tokenization before any Kokoro model had started training. - https://github.com/polm/cutlet - https://github.com/polm/fugashi - https://github.com/ikegami-yukino/jaconv - https://github.com/studio-ousia/mojimoji ### Korean The Korean tokenizer is copied from 5Hyeons's g2pkc fork of Kyubyong's widely used g2pK library. Deep gratitute to [@5Hyeons](https://github.com/5Hyeons) for kindly helping with Korean and extending the original code by [@Kyubyong](https://github.com/Kyubyong). - https://github.com/5Hyeons/StyleTTS2/tree/vocos/g2pK/g2pkc - https://github.com/Kyubyong/g2pK ### Chinese The second gen Chinese tokenizer adapts better logic from paddlespeech's frontend. Jieba now cuts and tags, and pinyin-to-ipa is no longer used. - https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleSpeech/tree/develop/paddlespeech/t2s/frontend The first gen Chinese tokenizer uses jieba to cut, pypinyin, and pinyin-to-ipa. - https://github.com/fxsjy/jieba - https://github.com/mozillazg/python-pinyin - https://github.com/stefantaubert/pinyin-to-ipa ### Vietnamese - https://github.com/v-nhandt21/Viphoneme ### TODO - [ ] Data: Compress [data](https://github.com/hexgrad/misaki/tree/main/misaki/data) (no need for indented json) and eliminate redundancy between gold and silver dictionaries. - [ ] Fallbacks: Train seq2seq fallback models on dictionaries using [this notebook](https://github.com/Kyubyong/nlp_made_easy/blob/master/PyTorch%20seq2seq%20template%20based%20on%20the%20g2p%20task.ipynb). - [ ] Homographs: Escalate hard words like `axes bass bow lead tear wind` using BERT contextual word embeddings (CWEs) and logistic regression (LR) models (`nn.Linear` followed by sigmoid) as described in [this paper](https://assets.amazon.science/c3/db/23ca18d7450d8dbb5b80a11fcdd3/homograph-disambiguation-with-contextual-word-embeddings-for-tts-systems.pdf). Assuming `trf=True`, BERT CWEs can be accessed via `doc._.trf_data`, see [en.py#L479](https://github.com/hexgrad/misaki/blob/main/misaki/en.py#L479). Per-word LR models can be trained on [WikipediaHomographData](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/WikipediaHomographData), [llama-hd-dataset](https://github.com/facebookresearch/llama-hd-dataset), and LLM-generated data. - [x] More languages: Add `ko.py`, `ja.py`, `zh.py`. - [x] Per-language pip installs ### Acknowledgements - 🛠️ Misaki builds on top of many excellent G2P projects linked above. - 🌐 Thank you to all native speakers who advised and contributed G2P in many languages. - 👾 Kokoro Discord server: https://discord.gg/QuGxSWBfQy - 🌸 Misaki is a Japanese name and a [character in the Terminator franchise](https://terminator.fandom.com/wiki/Misaki) along with [Kokoro](https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro?tab=readme-ov-file#acknowledgements).
